title: Summit Expedition
description: An online board game for math tutoring: students race up Mt. Axiom by solving problems at the difficulty they choose, and wrong answers never send anyone backward.
overview: Summit Expedition is an online board game for math tutoring where students race to climb Mt. Axiom by solving math problems. On each turn a player rolls a die, then chooses how hard a problem to take on: Safe, Bold or Daring. Harder problems move them farther up the trail when answered correctly. Wrong answers never send anyone backward. The student sees a worked solution and earns insight tokens that trade for power-up cards, such as a hint or a second try. Along the way there are supply caches, weather events, camps, and a risky Ice Ridge shortcut guarded by an Ice Wall.

Tutors choose which topics are in play, from Algebra 1 through Calculus, and problems are generated fresh each time. The difficulty adjusts quietly to how the student is doing. Tutor tools let you override answers, give retries or change topics mid-game. A session report at the end shows each student’s accuracy by skill and every problem they missed. Up to four players can climb, including the tutor, and it works over screen-share for online sessions anywhere.

title: Leverage Planner
description: A local-first planner that ranks what I could be doing by leverage against my own goals, then fits the best of it into my real day.
overview: A local-first personal strategy engine. It ranks everything I could be doing by leverage against my own goals, fits the best of it into my real day with sleep, meals, training and people protected, and compares that plan with what I'd otherwise do. Daily and weekly reviews feed back in, recalibrating time estimates and flagging when one goal is eating more than its share of the week. No accounts or API keys, and all data stays in the browser.
details: An eight-factor weighted leverage score, with a plain-language explanation for every ranking.
A scheduler that works around routine, commitments and travel, matches tasks to energy and focus windows, and stops before eating into requested open time.
Important tasks that don't fit come back with concrete fixes: postpone something lower-ranked, shorten, split or move to tomorrow.
After three completed tasks per goal, actual-vs-estimate ratios recalibrate future durations.
55 unit tests cover the scoring, scheduling, comparison and review engine.

title: Search and Rescue Debrief
description: Gathers and summarizes findings from numerous team members after a search mission, matching up debrief notes across the team to produce one accurate, consolidated summary of what happened.
overview: Each volunteer submits their own account of a mission through a structured questionnaire. Once every expected volunteer has submitted, the mission is ready for an AI-generated consensus debrief that reconciles where accounts agree and flags discrepancies for a mission lead to review.
details: Built so far: the data model, a shared questionnaire schema, mission creation, and the volunteer submission flow with automatic status tracking.
Next: AI consensus generation with the Claude API.

title: Mentor Update Letter Helper
description: Turns the notes I take on a student throughout the week into a casual, informative update letter for parents — covering academics, social growth, and athletics — without me rewriting it from scratch every Friday.

title: Lesson Differentiation Engine
description: A tool that takes a math or physics objective plus a real student's profile and has Claude generate three genuinely different lessons for it live, each with the learning-science reasoning behind it.
problem: Some students can't be reached by a lesson written for “the average student”, and differentiation is the answer — but writing one genuinely different version of a lesson, grounded in real learning science, can take longer than writing the original. Most teachers end up differentiating by instinct, without the bandwidth to do it well for more than one or two students at a time.
solution: Give the engine a real math or physics objective and a student profile, and Claude generates three structurally different instructional pathways live — each with a margin note explaining why it fits that student, grounded in executive-function and UDL research. The teacher still picks, adapts and knows the kid; the tool does the first draft of the reasoning.
details: The interface is drawn like a technical blueprint, because a lesson plan is an engineering problem: a fixed objective, real constraints, and a structure that gets from one to the other.
Next ideas: saving and editing pathways into a lesson library, a “why not” mode that names the approaches it avoided, and batching several students for one class period.

title: Used Bicycle Verification
description: Uses blockchain technology to continuously verify transactions in the used bicycle market, so buyers and sellers can trust a bike's ownership and sale history.
